title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation day on campus.


The first few weeks in the Master of Data Science in Computational Linguistics program have been exciting, challenging, and full of surprises. One of the most valuable things I learned during orientation came from alumni and instructors. They shared practical advice that can make a big difference, such as submitting assignments to Gradescope at least two hours before the deadline. At first, I did not fully understand why this was so important, but after spending hours troubleshooting PDF rendering and knitting errors, I quickly learned that technical issues often take longer than expected to resolve.
The pace of the program has been much faster than I anticipated. During the first week alone, we were introduced to new tools, workflows, and course expectations. Despite feeling overwhelmed at times, I found myself gradually adapting to the workload and becoming more comfortable with the technology. The labs have been especially helpful because they provide an opportunity to ask questions, review concepts, and catch up when things move quickly.
One of the biggest surprises was the teaching style in DSCI 523. The flipped classroom approach was very different from what I had experienced before. On the very first day, we started with a quiz in the first few minutes of class and then worked through a worksheet during the lecture. Although it felt challenging at first, I found that this approach encouraged active learning and helped me stay engaged. The experience has been demanding, but also interesting and rewarding, and I can already see how much I am learning from it.

Before joining UBC, I studied engineering in Egypt and worked as a Network Operations Center (NOC) Engineer, supporting enterprise networks and solving complex technical challenges. My professional experience sparked a growing interest in using data to understand patterns, generate insights, and support decision-making.
I am also a co-founder of StreetKey, a data-driven platform that explores neighborhood livability and safety using structured and unstructured data. This experience strengthened my passion for analytics, machine learning, and human-centered technology.

title: Mona Bekhit
text:
Hi! I’m Mona, a Master’s student in Data Science in Computational Linguistics at the University of British Columbia (UBC).
I grew up in Egypt, where I studied engineering and began my career in networking and telecommunications. Over the years, I worked as a Network Operations Center (NOC) Engineer, supporting large-scale enterprise networks and solving complex technical problems. My experience ranged from troubleshooting and network optimization to customer support and system operations across multinational organizations.
My interest in data science grew from a desire to move beyond maintaining systems and toward extracting insights from data to solve real-world problems. I became fascinated by how data can be transformed into meaningful stories and actionable decisions. This interest eventually led me to co-found StreetKey, a data-driven platform that explores neighborhood livability and safety using both structured and unstructured data sources. Working on StreetKey strengthened my passion for analytics, machine learning, and the power of data to improve everyday life.
Today, I’m pursuing Computational Linguistics because I’m particularly interested in the intersection of language, artificial intelligence, and human communication. I’m excited by the potential of natural language processing to help people access information, learn more effectively, and interact with technology in more natural ways.
Outside of data science, I’m a mother, mother of two, and lifelong learner. I enjoy swimming, going to the gym, creating Arabic children’s storytelling content on YouTube, and experimenting with voice-over projects. I also like exploring new technologies, and spending quality time with my family around Canada.
I’m always curious about how data, language, and technology can come together to create meaningful and human-centered solutions.
